name: Swiss Style
garments: not a fashion look — a graphic design movement
reacts_against: decorative, hand-lettered graphic design, insisting on strict grid systems, sans-serif type (Helvetica, released 1957, is its defining typeface) and objective, legible communication.
revivals: still the default grammar of most corporate and editorial graphic design

wiki_facts.key_motifs: Akzidenz-Grotesk, Univers and Helvetica fonts, asymmetric layouts, grids, limited color palettes
wiki_facts.key_values: Cleanliness, readibility, objectivity[https://www.printmag.com/featured/swiss-style-principles-typefaces-designers/ "Swiss Style: The Principles, the Typefaces & the Designers" | printmag.com]

findings: dark — about 47% of the measured color across 6 wiki photos is below mid-lightness
a vivid streak — roughly 27% of the color measured is highly saturated
mostly muted — about 60% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from the Aesthetics Wiki images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
